name: trend-family-beyond-5h-horizons
rationale: Literature-motivated. The composite's trend family (SMA cross, EMA cross, MACD histogram, weight 0.25 each vs 1.0 for RSI/Bollinger) currently runs at 1-minute horizons of 200 / 100 / 12-26-9 bars, i.e. 3.3h / 1.7h / 12-26 minutes -- all inside the sub-5h regime where Tang et al. measure Bitcoin as subdiffusive (mean-reverting). A trend signal measured there is fighting the reversion family and adding churn: 2026-09-21's `contrarian-composite-inversion` and 2026-09-22's `contrarian-trend-subsignals`/`trend-weight-half` results show the trend terms at current horizons carry no edge. This moves every trend-family period beyond the ~5h crossover into the superdiffusive (trending) regime: SMA 1440 (24h), EMA 720 (12h), MACD 360/780/270 (6h/13h/4.5h). Reversion-family periods and all weights are unchanged. Note: run with --warmup-candles 1500 (SMA 1440 needs >= 1440 warmup bars; MACD slow+signal = 1050); warmup is excluded from the report so the evaluated window is identical to the baseline's.

paper_reference.title: Stylized Facts of High-Frequency Bitcoin Time Series
paper_reference.authors: Yaoyue Tang, Karina Arias-Calluari, Mohammad-Reza Najafi, Michael S. Harré, Fernando Alonso-Marroquin
paper_reference.key_claim: In 2021-2022 BTC/USD 10-minute data, price diffusion is subdiffusive (H = 0.478, mean-reverting) at short intervals and weakly superdiffusive (H = 0.646, trending) beyond roughly 5 hours.
paper_reference.pros: Directly states the horizon at which trend-following should start to work on BTC, which maps one-to-one onto shirube's trend-family period parameters, and is consistent with this pipeline's own finding that short-horizon reversion dominates.
paper_reference.cons: BTC/USD aggregate data, not bitFlyer BTC/JPY; ends May 2022, before the ETF-era liquidity regime; a descriptive Hurst-exponent study with no trading rule, fees or out-of-sample test; the ~5h crossover is regime-dependent (their earlier period differs). Used only to pick which side of 5h to test, not to predict a Sharpe.
